claim: Real-world Netdata agents on Debian 10/11 (v1.36.1) used 200-1000+ MB RAM, and one practitioner measured 2.5 GB reserved / 1.4 GB used on 16 GB hosts collecting ~7500 metrics, despite docs promising under 100 MB.
stance_target: The claim that heavyweight monitoring agents are cheap enough to run on every fleet host without resource tuning
scope_conditions: Netdata 1.36.1/1.37-era, Debian 10/11 and CentOS 9 Stream, dbengine mode, 2022-2023; practitioner forum reports corroborated by Netdata founder
quoted_support: Installed "default", had some insane memory usage for netdata daemon. From 200-400 MB for regular servers to 700-1000+MB for kvm hypervisors. USED memory. And that's just in a single month. ... I'm facing a similar issue where the agents are using 2.5GB of RAM a few seconds after restarting the service on nodes that only come with 16GB of RAM.

claim: Netdata's founder confirmed dbengine's in-memory index is the main memory offender and recommended a production-child config of [db] mode=alloc retention=1800, storage tiers=1, [ml] enabled=no, [health] enabled=no, yielding under 50 MB RAM per child that streams to Parent nodes.
stance_target: Edge-light/centralised-heavy architecture as the pattern for jupiterOS fleet agents
scope_conditions: Netdata agent, production child nodes, v1.36-era defaults before dbengine v2
quoted_support: Generally, on production systems you should use (in netdata.conf) something like this: [db] storage tiers = 1, mode = alloc, retention = 1800 ... [ml] enabled = no ... [health] enabled = no. With these settings, netdata should not use more than 50MB of RAM.

claim: dbengine v2 (merged January 2023, shipped in v1.37) reduced a default-config Netdata agent on 64-bit machines to about 100 MB RAM with 3 storage tiers and about 1 year retention, and the journal-file PR #13885 reduced dbengine memory footprint by 80-90% at a cost of 15% speed and 10% disk.
stance_target: How much engineering effort incumbent agents spent to reach a ~100 MB fleet footprint
quoted_support: A Netdata Agent running with default settings on a 64 bit machine should now use about 100MB of RAM, using 3 storage tiers, providing about 1 year of data retention ... this reduces the memory footprint of dbengine by 80 - 90%, while sacrificing just 15% of its speed and 10% of disk space.

claim: A confirmed ARAL array-allocator memory leak magnified Netdata's memory consumption (fixed October 2022), and a separate leak on CentOS 9 Stream (issue #14288) was traced to the ebpf.plugin, which the maintainer recommended disabling.
stance_target: Evidence that heavyweight agents carry reliability risk from complex plugin subsystems (eBPF), relevant to ha-linux-agent's reliability critique
quoted_support: And we found a memory leak in the way dbengine allocated memory, so we also had a leak magnifying the problem. ... this line show on 2 machine where leak happens: systemd-coredump ... (ebpf.plugin) of user 986 dumped core.
